historicalCorrection.author: gpt-6
historicalCorrection.reason: XXII.2 supports accession/entry; XXII.5.2 supports temple and sacrifice policy. Broadened working date to December361–early362 rather than assert one reopening day. Ammianus admires Julian but also criticizes him; neither admiration, hostile generalizations nor inferred policy motives become the objective narrator’s own judgment. Civic logistics are fiction, not actual temple construction or a decree enforcement counter.

consultations.coverageActuallyRead: Architect directly read selected entry/accession chapter2 and religious policy5.1–4 in the displayed English edition; adjacent criticisms recognized as context, not wholebook reading.
consultations.limitations: Later fourth-century narrator and former officer, not a neutral stenographer of the palace. Entry11December in this edition; use broad working frame for subsequent policy. Reopening/sacrifice orders do not quantify each local temple, acceptance or practice. Christian discord and imperial calculation in5.4 remain attributed interpretation; no recycled hostile generalization or authentic dialogue.
